html:
A concrete arch dam on the Zambezi between today's Zambia and Zimbabwe, built from 1955 to 1959. Behind it lies Lake Kariba, one of the largest reservoirs in the world by volume.

It was the showpiece of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, and an Italian firm built it. Its power went to the copper mines of the Copperbelt and the cities of Southern Rhodesia.

The lake flooded the valley home of about 57,000 Tonga people, who were moved, some by force, to poorer land. In Tonga belief the river spirit Nyaminyami was angered; great floods during construction killed workers and were read as his answer. As the water rose, a rescue known as Operation Noah saved thousands of stranded animals.

The dam still supplies much of the power of both countries. Ghana's Akosombo Dam, built a few years later, made a lake of even larger area.
sum: A concrete arch dam on the Zambezi between today's Zambia and Zimbabwe, built from 1955 to 1959. Behind it lies Lake Kariba, one of the largest reservoirs in the world by volume.
